info.name: IAM Service — Auth API
info.description:
Exercises every /api/v1/auth endpoint in app/api/v1/routes/auth.py, plus the org scaffolding needed to reach switch-tenant/accept-invite. Sibling to the ../users and ../tenants collections — kept separate so each can be run/maintained independently.

**Known gaps vs. the Authentication API Specification doc (flagged so they don't look like collection bugs):**
- The spec's MFA-verify step is `POST /auth/verify-mfa` with `{challenge_token, otp}`. The real route is `POST /auth/mfa/login-verify` with `{mfa_challenge_token, code}` — this collection uses the real one.
- `POST /auth/logout`, `/change-password`, and `/reset-password` return `204 No Content` here, not the spec's `{success, message}` body.
- `POST /auth/login` now accepts the spec's optional `client`/`context` metadata blocks (every field within them optional too) — `client.device_name`/`browser`/`platform` override the User-Agent-derived `session.device`; `context` is accepted but otherwise informational only (never trusted over the real connection IP). `POST /auth/register` still doesn't accept them, nor `confirm_password` — extra fields there are silently ignored by FastAPI.
- The real JWT access-token payload carries `sub/type/tenant_id/role/is_superuser/iat/exp/jti` — no `permissions` array baked into the token itself (permissions are resolved server-side per-request). The 'Login — Success' request's Test script decodes and asserts the real claim set.
- `tenant_id` (org slug) and `role` (display name) are deliberately **not** duplicated in the login response body — `body.user.tenant`/`body.user.role` only carry `id`/`name` fields the token itself doesn't have; the same values on the token are read by decoding it (see 'Login Primary User (tenant A)' and 'Switch Tenant'). `POST /auth/switch-tenant`'s response is just `{access_token}` for the same reason. `is_superuser` is JWT-only too — never in any response body (register's Common User Object is the one exception, by design).
- `forgot-password`'s `reset_token`, `register`'s `verification_token`, and an organization invitation's `invitation_token` are only ever returned in the HTTP response when the server runs with `DEBUG=true` (there's no email/notification provider wired up). Without it, '1. Registration' > Verify Email, '4. Password Management' > Reset Password, and '5. Tenant Switching & Invitations' > Accept Invite degrade gracefully (tolerant assertions + a console note) instead of failing the run.

**Prerequisites (same as the ../users collection):**
1. Run the service: `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000`.
2. Create a superuser: `uv run python scripts/create_superuser.py admin@example.com ChangeMe123!` (update `superuser_email`/`superuser_password` below if different).
3. Optional but recommended for full coverage: set `DEBUG=true` in `services/iam/.env` before starting the server, so reset_token/verification_token/invitation_token are revealed (see gaps above).

**Auto token handling:** identical pattern to the ../users collection — Login/Register Test scripts capture `access_token`/`refresh_token` per actor into collection variables, and a collection-level pre-request script auto-refreshes a near-expired token via `POST /auth/refresh` before any other request runs.

**MFA testing:** TOTP codes are computed live in pre-request scripts from the `secret` returned by `POST /auth/mfa/setup`, using a pure-JS RFC 6238 implementation (Postman's built-in CryptoJS for HMAC-SHA1 + a base32 decoder) — no manual code entry needed to exercise Confirm MFA / Verify MFA Login / Disable MFA.

**Run order matters** — folders build on each other (Setup creates two organizations the Primary User belongs to; MFA enables/disables on that same account; Logout is last because it blacklists the access token and revokes the refresh-token family immediately).

exec: // Collection-level: auto-detect a near-expired/missing access token for
// the current actor(s) and silently refresh it via POST /auth/refresh
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ refresh_token: refreshToken }) }
console.log('[auto-refresh] ' + actor + ' refresh skipped/failed (continuing with existing token)');
// Requests whose own Test script defines/rotates a token manage it
// directly — skip auto-refresh for those so we don't step on them.

item.name: 0. Setup
item.description: Bootstraps a logged-in superuser plus a 'Primary User' who belongs to two organizations (org A and org B) — needed later for the ambiguous-tenant-login, switch-tenant, and MFA-during-login demos.

request.description: Requires the account named by superuser_email/superuser_password to already exist with is_superuser=true — see the collection description for scripts/create_superuser.py.

Real request body is {email, password, full_name} only — the spec's confirm_password/tenant/client/context fields aren't accepted by RegisterRequest (FastAPI silently ignores unknown fields, so they're omitted here rather than implied to do something).

item.name: 6. Logout
item.description: Run this LAST — logout blacklists the access token's jti and revokes the entire refresh-token family immediately, so member_access_token/member_refresh_token are unusable for the rest of the collection afterward.

request.description: Real response is 204 No Content, not the spec's {success, message} body. Relies on Postman's per-domain cookie jar to also send the httponly refresh_token cookie set by the last Login/Switch Tenant call, in addition to the bearer access token, so both the refresh-token family and the access token's jti get invalidated.
